citations.title: Facility licensure
citations.requirement: APD licenses group home facilities (4-15 residents) and foster care facilities (3 or fewer). The statute requires Level 2 screening of the applicant, managers, supervisors and direct service staff (subsec. (5)). It requires proof of financial ability (subsec. (6)) and a comprehensive emergency management plan (subsec. (8)). It requires an annual sworn statement of costs for APD-funded clients (subsec. (10)). APD cannot fund an unlicensed facility.

citations.title: License Application and Renewal Procedures (amended 3-26-26)
citations.requirement: Each home has its own license (subsec. (8)). The application is complete only with all documents, screenings and a satisfactory inspection. Deficiencies must be corrected before the license issues. Renewals are due at least 45 days before expiration (subsec. (4)); late or incomplete renewals are treated as initial applications. Give APD 30 days' written notice before closing a home (subsec. (13)).

citations.title: Length of Licenses
citations.requirement: Residential facility licenses are issued for one year.

citations.title: Agency Monitoring and Oversight
citations.requirement: APD monitors licensed homes at least monthly, including one weekend visit a year (subsec. (4)). It may request proof of ability to operate 60 days without state payment (subsec. (5)). It reviews the home on site within 30 days after the first admission (subsec. (8)).

citations.title: Licensed Residential Facility Capacity
citations.requirement: APD sets licensed capacity and resident characteristics. Capacity changes must be requested 30 days ahead with a passed fire inspection and zoning compliance (subsec. (1)(d)). Census changes must be reported in writing (subsec. (2)). Serve only residents whose characteristics match the license (subsec. (3)).

citations.title: General Residential Facility Standards
citations.requirement: Physical plant standards: no mobile homes; maximum 2 residents per bedroom for homes first licensed on or after 7/1/2014; bedroom space of at least 80 sq ft (single) or 60 sq ft per person (shared); one toilet, sink and tub/shower per 3 residents; 35 sq ft of living/dining space per household member; hot water at or below 120°F; smoke and CO detectors; restricted access to water hazards; secured hazardous chemicals; meal provisions; an office area with secure records storage.

citations.title: Group Home Facility Standards
citations.requirement: The facility operator needs 90 college credits in a related field, or a high school diploma plus 3 years of disability experience. The operator must be on site or on call at all times, with a designated backup (subsecs. (2)-(3)). The home needs a designated office area (subsec. (4)).

citations.title: Staffing Requirements for Residential Facilities (amended 3-26-26)
citations.requirement: The licensee must employ adequate staff for the number and characteristics of residents, even above the minimum (subsec. (1)). DSP qualifications are in subsec. (2): age 18+; ch. 435 / s. 393.0655 screening; high school diploma or equivalent; 1 year of experience or 30 semester hours / 45 quarter hours / 720 classroom hours of related training. Subsec. (2)(f)-(h) sets the supervised 90-day alternative, written notice to the Regional Office within 5 days of hire, and a performance evaluation within 120 days. Subsec. (3) sets required skills. Subsec. (4) covers fitness for duty, driver standards (no qualifying violation in 3 years, annual driving-history update) and the annual FDLE sexual offender/predator database check within one mile. Subsec. (5) covers investigations. Subsec. (6) covers personnel records, job descriptions, weekly schedules posted one week ahead and actual schedules kept 6 months; copies go to APD within 3 calendar days. Subsec. (7) sets training: Direct Care Core Competencies and classroom CPR/first aid within 90 days, Zero Tolerance before services with refresher every 3 years, HIV/AIDS within 90 days, behavior-plan training by a certified behavior analyst, and Ch. 65G-8 compliance. Training records are kept 3 years.

citations.title: Resident Care and Supervision Standards (amended 3-26-26)
citations.requirement: Subsec. (1) covers care standards, the Bill of Rights, written house rules and follow-up of medical appointments. Subsec. (2) requires community activity opportunities. Subsec. (3) covers admission/termination criteria, notice to APD before accepting each new resident and a census change report within 5 calendar days. It also covers transfer approval and the property inventory. Subsec. (4) covers resident funds. Subsec. (5) covers resident records: contents, updated within 30 days of new information, retained 6 years, copies to APD within 2 calendar days. Subsec. (6) requires at least one staff present at all times residents are in the facility, with limited exceptions by Regional Office-approved plan. Subsec. (7) covers video monitoring. Subsec. (8) covers behavioral interventions. Subsec. (9) covers the sexual activity policy and Safety Plan safeguards. Subsec. (10) covers solicitation. Subsec. (11) covers first aid. Subsec. (12) covers medication. Subsec. (13) covers specialized equipment. Subsec. (14) covers transportation. Subsec. (15) covers staff communication.

citations.title: Fire and Emergency Procedures (amended 3-26-26)
citations.requirement: Subsec. (1) requires emergency numbers at every phone extension. Subsec. (2) requires an annual fire inspection under ch. 69A-38 and an approved inspection before initial licensure or renewal. Subsec. (3) requires monthly fire drills, with records kept 1 year and no drills between midnight and 5:00 a.m. Subsec. (4) covers the CEMP: reviewed/updated annually, staff trained within 30 days of hire and annually, evacuation reported to the Regional Office within 6 hours and every 6 hours after, emergency shelter over-capacity reported within 48 hours. Subsec. (5) covers missing residents. Subsec. (6) covers incident reporting: Abuse Hotline immediately; APD Incident Reporting Form OP 3-0006 (Dec. 2025); initial notice of a critical incident within 4 hours and the completed form within 1 calendar day; reportable incidents within 1 calendar day; follow-up within 5 days.

citations.title: Siting; site selection of community residential homes
citations.requirement: No more than three APD facilities within 1,000 ft (rule subsec. (4)). Homes of 6 or fewer residents are a single-family use. Homes of 7-14 residents must be in multifamily zoning, and local government has 60 days to approve or deny. Notify zoning when the home receives its first resident.

citations.title: Personal Needs Allowance; Room and Board Payment
citations.requirement: The personal needs allowance is at least 18% of the SSI federal benefit rate ($178.92/month at the 2026 SSI rate of $994). APD room-and-board standard is $583.42/month. Claim room and board on Form 65G-13.008A within 90 days after month end.

citations.title: Medication administration training and validation
citations.requirement: Unlicensed staff may administer medication only after the APD Basic Medication Administration course (exam of at least 85%; 100% on the MAR section) and validation by an approved validator. They must complete an annual update and revalidation, and revalidate within the 60 days before expiry. Ch. 65G-7 is also incorporated by 65G-2.009(12)(e)-(f) for the daily medication record, storage and error reporting.

citations.title: Administration of medication
citations.requirement: An unlicensed direct service provider may supervise self-administration or administer oral, transdermal, ophthalmic, otic, rectal, inhaled, enteral or topical prescription medications only after an initial course of at least 6 hours by an agency-approved trainer. Validation is onsite with an actual client and medication, initially and annually, for oral, enteral, ophthalmic, rectal and inhaled routes. Otic, transdermal and topical routes are validated by simulation in the initial course. An annual 2-hour in-service on medication administration and error prevention is required. A provider who misses revalidation or the in-service must repeat the initial course. APD must set procedures by rule.

citations.title: Screening of direct service providers
citations.requirement: Level 2 employment screening under ch. 435 is required for direct service providers, managers and supervisors of licensed residential facilities, and anyone with access to residents' living areas, funds or property. Exemptions from disqualification only as provided in s. 435.07. Disqualifying offenses include those listed in the statute.

citations.title: Care Provider Background Screening Clearinghouse
citations.requirement: Screening results are managed through the AHCA Care Provider Background Screening Clearinghouse. Employers register and track eligibility there.

citations.title: Treatment of persons with developmental disabilities (Bill of Rights)
citations.requirement: Rights in subsec. (3) apply to all persons with developmental disabilities. They include dignity, privacy and humane care; freedom from abuse, neglect, exploitation and unnecessary restraint, isolation or excessive medication; religious freedom; social interaction and community participation; exercise and recreation; the right to consent to or refuse treatment, subject to a guardian advocate (s. 393.12) or guardian (ch. 744); and no discrimination in publicly funded programs. No behavioral program may be implemented unless reviewed under APD rule. Clients have the right to be free from unnecessary restraint or seclusion, and APD adopts rules limiting its use. Confirm the current subsection numbering against the 2025 statute.

citations.title: Reactive Strategies
citations.requirement: Providers that use reactive strategies need an APD-approved emergency procedure curriculum (65G-8.002): at least 12 direct training hours, a written test with an 80% minimum score, and certification valid for one year. Staff must be certified before using any technique. 65G-8.003 requires policies and procedures, an annual internal review and consent information in client records. 65G-8.008 covers chemical restraint. 65G-8.009 lists prohibited procedures. 65G-8.010 covers documentation and notification. Cited text is the 2008 adoption; APD has draft revisions in development, so confirm the current text before finalizing.

citations.title: Service Delivery Practice and Procedure - Behavior Analysis Services
citations.requirement: Behavior analysis services with restricted procedures are provided or supervised by a certified behavior analyst. Written plans go to the Local Review Committee (LRC) chair within 5 working days after implementation (65G-4.010(1)). The LRC reviews, approves or disapproves plans. Disapproved plans are revised and resubmitted within 14 working days (65G-4.008). Cited text is the 4/4/2012 rule; confirm current text.

citations.cite: Rule 59G-13.070, F.A.C. (iBudget Waiver Services Coverage and Limitations Handbook, May 2023)
citations.title: iBudget Waiver Services Coverage and Limitations Handbook
citations.requirement: Residential Habilitation (handbook pp. 2-46 to 2-65). Minimum direct-care hours per resident per 24 hours: Basic 2, Minimal 4, Moderate 6, Extensive 1 8, Extensive 2 11. The provider bills the monthly rate for 24 or more days in the home and the daily rate otherwise. Provider qualifications are on p. 1-20; Appendix B covers training and APD iConnect. Behavior focus and intensive behavioral designations (p. 2-48) require BCBA or Ch. 490/491 monitoring (p. 2-52) and staff training (pp. 2-52 to 2-53). The handbook requires the implementation plan, quarterly summary and annual report. The Medicaid Waiver Services Agreement is AHCA Form 5000-3553.

citations.title: iBudget Waiver Services Provider Rate Table
citations.requirement: Rates are set by support level and county group. The Oct. 1, 2025 table is incorporated; a July 2026 table (about +1.0% for residential habilitation) is in rule development (Notice 31315303).

citations.title: HCBS settings requirements
citations.requirement: Provider-owned or controlled residential settings need a lease or equivalent agreement, lockable bedroom doors, roommate choice, access to food and visitors, freedom to decorate, and documented person-centered justification for any modification (subsec. (c)(4)).

citations.title: Definitions
citations.requirement: A foster care facility has 3 or fewer residents. A group home facility has 4-15 residents. No new residential habilitation centers are licensed.

citations.title: Change of Ownership; License Violations (non-disciplinary and disciplinary); License Denial, Suspension or Revocation
citations.requirement: These rules, all effective 3/26/2026, govern change of ownership, violation classes and fines, and license denial, suspension or revocation. Chapter 65G-2 also repealed 65G-2.017 (Health Safety Standards) and 65G-2.014 effective 3/26/2026. Rule titles and effective dates are verified; read the full rule text before drafting detailed procedures.

citations.cite: s. 448.110, F.S.; Fla. Const. art. X, s. 24
citations.title: Florida Minimum Wage
citations.requirement: Florida minimum wage is $15.00/hour from Sept. 30, 2026.

citations.title: Workers' compensation definitions
citations.requirement: Workers' compensation coverage is required for employers with four or more employees.

citations.cite: ss. 39.201 and 415.1034, F.S. (as incorporated by Rule 65G-2.010(6)(a), F.A.C.)
citations.title: Mandatory reporting of abuse, neglect and exploitation
citations.requirement: Known or suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation is reported immediately to the Florida Abuse Hotline, 1-800-962-2873. The citation is verified as it appears in the text of 65G-2.010(6)(a); statute text was not independently fetched.

policies.title: Organization, Governing Body and Facility Operator/Program Director Responsibilities
state_specifics: Licensed type is Group Home Facility (4-15 residents) or Foster Care Facility (3 or fewer), licensed under s. 393.067 and Ch. 65G-2.
Facility operator must hold 90 college credits in a related field, or a high school diploma plus 3 years of disability experience (65G-2.0072).
Operator is on site or on call at all times, with a designated backup for absences.
The licensee is responsible for adequate staffing above the minimum when residents need more (65G-2.008(1)(b)).
The governing body or owner must receive the annual cost statement and review it before filing.

policies.title: Licensure, Waiver Provider Enrollment and Provider Agreements
state_specifics: Two tracks: APD facility license (one year; each home licensed separately) and iBudget waiver enrollment (APD listing letter, AHCA Medicaid enrollment, then the Medicaid Waiver Services Agreement, AHCA Form 5000-3553).
Renew each license at least 45 days before expiration; late or incomplete renewals become initial applications (65G-2.002(4)).
An approved annual fire inspection is a prerequisite for initial licensure and each renewal (65G-2.010(2)).
Give APD 30 days' written notice before closing a home (65G-2.002(13)).
No license fee appears on Form 65G-2.002-A (Dec. 2025).
Keep local zoning notified; notify zoning when the first resident is placed.

policies.title: Policy Review and Document Control
state_specifics: Required written policies include: admission/termination criteria (65G-2.009(3)(a)), resident funds (2.009(4)(b)), behavioral responses (2.009(8)(a)), sexual activity (2.009(9)(a)), and video monitoring criteria if used (2.009(7)(b)).
Submit policies and procedures with the APD agency provider application and with the license application.
Ch. 65G-8 requires an annual internal review of emergency/reactive-strategy procedures (65G-8.003(6)).
Review the CEMP at least annually (65G-2.010(4)(b)).
Chapter 65G-2 rules were largely amended 3/26/2026; keep a rule-change log.

policies.title: Quality Improvement, Data Review and Mortality Review
federal: 42 CFR 441.302(a)(6) (HCBS assurances: monitoring of health and welfare)
state_specifics: Review all APD incident reports (OP 3-0006) and follow-up actions, including preventive measures to avoid recurrence (65G-2.010(6)(h)).
Review reactive-strategy and medication-error data; staff retraining is required when there is evidence of medication errors (65G-2.009(12)(a)).
Review the annual emergency procedure evaluation (65G-8.003(6)).
Any unexpected death is a critical incident, reported within 4 hours.
Review each death for contributing factors; record the review in the QI file.

policies.title: Medicaid Compliance, Billing and Service Documentation (iConnect)
state_specifics: Bill only services covered by a Waiver Support Coordinator-issued authorization.

Bill the monthly rate when the individual is in the home 24 or more days in the month; otherwise bill the daily rate. Submit after month end. Never bill days the individual was absent (handbook p. 2-50).
Staff the home to at least the handbook minimum direct-care hours per resident per day (Basic 2 / Minimal 4 / Moderate 6 / Extensive 1 8 / Extensive 2 11).
APD iConnect access requires iConnect training with a score of 75% or more (Handbook App. B).
EVV in iConnect applies to personal care and home health, not residential habilitation; confirm in the current handbook.
Claim APD room and board on Form 65G-13.008A within 90 days after month end.
Rates follow Rule 59G-13.081; check for the July 2026 table.

policies.title: Change of Ownership, Census, Capacity and Closure Notices
state_specifics: Notify APD before accepting each new resident (65G-2.009(3)(c)).
Report census changes in writing within 5 calendar days (65G-2.009(3)(g); 65G-2.006(2)).
Request capacity changes 30 days ahead, with a passed fire inspection and zoning compliance (65G-2.006(1)(d)).
Give APD 30 days' written notice before closing a home (65G-2.002(13)).
A licensee operating more than one facility needs APD approval before transferring a resident between its own facilities, except in an emergency (65G-2.009(3)(h)).
Change of ownership follows Rule 65G-2.0021.

policies.title: APD Monitoring, Inspections and Corrective Action
state_specifics: APD monitors licensed homes at least monthly, including one weekend visit per year; the 30-day post-admission review is on site (65G-2.0032).
Resident records must be available to APD staff with state ID for inspection and duplication; provide a complete copy as soon as possible and no later than 2 calendar days (65G-2.009(5)(f)).
Provide personnel records, schedules and training documentation to APD within 3 calendar days of request (65G-2.008(6)(b)).
Regional Office staff may observe fire drills (65G-2.010(3)(c)).
Designate a custodian for monitoring-day document production; track violations and corrective actions per 65G-2.004, .0041 and .005.

policies.title: Individual Rights and HCBS Settings Requirements
state_specifics: Honor the Bill of Rights under s. 393.13, including dignity, privacy, religious freedom, no unnecessary restraint, community participation and the right to vote (65G-2.009(1)(b)).
Placement does not terminate or restrict the rights of parents or guardians (65G-2.009(1)(c)).
Provide a lease or equivalent residency agreement, lockable bedroom doors with key control, roommate choice, visitor and food access, freedom to decorate and to control own schedule.
Post or give each resident a copy of the Bill of Rights (APD publishes one) and list the Abuse Hotline number.
Encourage, but do not require, chores appropriate to age and ability (65G-2.009(1)(a)7).

policies.title: Rights Restrictions and Due Process
state_specifics: No behavioral program may be implemented unless it is reviewed under APD rules (Local Review Committee process, Ch. 65G-4).
Restraint and seclusion are limited to Ch. 65G-8 and are never for punishment or staff convenience.

Any restriction of an HCBS right requires a documented justification, less-intrusive alternatives tried, informed consent, and periodic review in the person-centered plan (42 CFR 441.301(c)(4)(vi)(F)).
Residents and legal representatives must be told they may challenge a restriction.
Remote video monitoring is barred in bedrooms and bathrooms (65G-2.009(7)(c)).

policies.title: Grievances and Complaints
state_specifics: Allegations of abuse, neglect or exploitation go to the Florida Abuse Hotline, 1-800-962-2873, not through the internal grievance process.
Post the Hotline number and the Regional Office contact (also required at each phone extension).
Residents, guardians and support coordinators may raise concerns with the Waiver Support Coordinator or APD Regional Office.
Provide notice of Medicaid fair hearing rights when services are denied, reduced, suspended or terminated.
Resident government and house-rule consultation is one avenue for resident concerns (65G-2.009(1)(d)-(e)).

policies.title: Privacy, Confidentiality and HIPAA
state_specifics: Resident and client records are confidential under s. 393.13 (65G-2.009(5)(e)).
Records stay on premises or electronically in a central location; cash and current financial information are secured (65G-2.009(4)(h)).
Retain a copy of records 6 years in accordance with HIPAA (65G-2.009(5)(g)).
Records must be open to APD and State of Florida agents with ID (65G-2.009(5)(f)).
Respect privacy and self-determination to the maximum extent possible during supervision (65G-2.009(6)(a)); knock before entering bedrooms.
Written consent is needed before use of image, name or information for fundraising (65G-2.009(10)).

policies.title: Personal Funds, Personal Needs Allowance and Property Management
state_specifics: Neither the licensee nor staff may gain financial benefit by charging fees against, borrowing, or using a resident's funds (65G-2.009(4)(a)).
Get written authorization signed by the resident or legal representative annually if the licensee manages funds (65G-2.009(4)(c)).
Keep written receipts for purchases of $25.00 or more for at least one year (65G-2.009(4)(d)).
Keep a monthly accounting per resident: balance, each deposit and withdrawal, purpose, staff name and signature, and resident signature for withdrawals the resident uses at own discretion.
Reconcile the available amount to the most recent ending balance (65G-2.009(4)(e)).
Keep cash accounting on separate forms. Where benefits are received, maintain a checking or savings account; no commingling with funds of anyone but other residents (65G-2.009(4)(f)-(g)).
Staff with access to funds must be trained on the procedures (65G-2.009(4)(b)).
Prohibited: being named beneficiary of a resident's life insurance unless related by blood or marriage; borrowing resident funds (65G-2.009(4)(j)).
PNA of at least 18% of the SSI FBR ($178.92 in 2026).

Complete an itemized property inventory on admission, signed by licensee and resident or representative. Update it within 30 days of new items, every 12 months and 30 days before discharge (65G-2.009(3)(j)4, (5)(d)).

policies.title: Informed Consent and Decision-Making Support
state_specifics: Right to consent to or refuse treatment, subject to a guardian advocate (s. 393.12) or guardian (ch. 744) (65G-2.009(1)(b)8).
Record guardianship status, legal competency and authorized representatives in the record (65G-2.009(5)(c)6).
Get written authorization for routine medical or dental care (65G-2.009(5)(c)4).
Written consent is required for video monitoring (65G-2.009(7)(b)3) and reactive-strategy consent is kept in the record (65G-8.003(1)).
Medication administered by unlicensed staff requires consent under s. 393.506; confirm current consent subsection.

policies.title: Nondiscrimination and Communication Access
federal: Title VI, Civil Rights Act (45 CFR 80)
state_specifics: Residents may not be excluded or denied benefits because of a developmental disability (65G-2.009(1)(b)9).
DSPs must be capable of effective communication with residents, support coordinators, APD staff and families (65G-2.008(3)(a)).
The facility must meet each resident's programmatic and physical accessibility needs before admission (65G-2.009(3)(d)).
Provide interpreters or alternate formats at no cost where needed, including language access for guardians.

policies.title: House Rules, Resident Government and Community Activities
state_specifics: Establish and make available to residents and employees written house rules, developed in consultation with residents (65G-2.009(1)(d)).
Help establish resident government when appropriate (65G-2.009(1)(e); s. 393.13).
Provide opportunities to participate in community activities (65G-2.009(2)).
Encourage public transportation where available and appropriate (65G-2.009(14)(o)).

policies.title: Video Monitoring and Surveillance
state_specifics: Video cameras are permitted, but footage may not be used to humiliate, punish, demean or violate privacy (65G-2.009(7)(a)).

A licensee using video must have written criteria for which residents are monitored and written protocols: who may access footage, purpose, and how, when and where it is stored (minimum 30-day retention).
Obtain written consent from the resident, or the guardian or legal representative, before use; explain when and where monitoring occurs.
Give APD the titles and positions of everyone with off-site access, with firewalls or equivalent safeguards.
Preserve footage for 30 days; after a critical incident captured on video; on notice of a law enforcement or DCF investigation; and at APD request.

Remote interactive monitoring is limited to vocational and educational settings, medical/special treatment spaces, administrative offices and common areas; never bedrooms or bathrooms (65G-2.009(7)(c)).
Video is a facility record available to APD. Storage inadequacy is not a defense. APD may restrict or suspend video monitoring (65G-2.009(7)(d)-(f)).
The (7) bedroom restriction has been subject to variance petitions in 2025-2026; do not install bedroom cameras without a granted variance.

policies.title: Use of Resident Name, Image and Information; Solicitation
state_specifics: Obtain written permission from the resident, if competent, or the legal representative before using the resident's image, voice, name, picture, personal information or disability to secure donations (65G-2.009(10)).
Apply the same consent standard to marketing materials and websites; keep signed releases in the individual's record.

policies.title: Referral, Admission and Transition In
state_specifics: Have written admission and termination criteria (also required in the license application) (65G-2.009(3)(a)).
Serve only persons with developmental disabilities, whether or not they are APD clients (65G-2.009(3)(b)).
Notify APD before accepting each new resident (65G-2.009(3)(c)).
Do not accept a person unless the facility can meet programmatic and physical accessibility needs and the placement does not harm current residents (65G-2.009(3)(d)-(e)).
Get APD approval before any placement that deviates from the characteristics (level of care, age, sex) on the license application.
For a non-APD-client, give APD documentation of developmental disability under Ch. 65G-4, medical needs, behavioral issues and known criminal history.
Before admission, review any Safety Plan (65G-2.009(9)(c)2).
Before placement, allow a visit by the individual and representative, cooperate with the Waiver Support Coordinator, brief staff, and complete the property inventory (65G-2.009(3)(j)).
Admissions come through Waiver Support Coordinator referrals and APD regional crisis placements; services start only after an authorization.

policies.title: Person-Centered Planning and Support Plan Coordination with the Waiver Support Coordinator
state_specifics: Keep a copy of the current support plan, as supplied by the Waiver Support Coordinator, in the record (65G-2.009(5)(c)10).
Facilitate implementation of support plans, behavior plans and directions from medical professionals (65G-2.009(1)(a)1).
Contact the support coordinator as needed for timely medical and dental care; if none is assigned, contact the legal representative (65G-2.009(1)(a)3-4).
Provide individualized care reflecting personal goals, abilities, sex, age and special needs (65G-2.009(1)(a)5).
Participate in staff training and meetings as APD requires (65G-2.009(1)(a)6).

policies.title: Implementation of Supports, Implementation Plan and Daily Documentation
state_specifics: Write an implementation plan for each resident, developed with the resident and tied to support plan goals (handbook, p. 2-48).
File quarterly summaries and an annual report with the Waiver Support Coordinator.
Keep implementation and behavior plans in the individual record (65G-2.009(5)(c)10).
Records must be current and updated at least 30 days after receipt of new information; document diligent effort if required information is unavailable (65G-2.009(5)(d)).
All documentation must be in legible English (65G-2.009(5)(b)).
Follow through on health care appointments: schedule follow-ups and train staff on any changes in medication, diet, positioning or equipment (65G-2.009(1)(f)).

policies.title: Community Integration and Employment Choice
state_specifics: Provide opportunities for community activities (65G-2.009(2)) and social interaction, exercise and recreation (s. 393.13).
Incidental transportation is provided as a typical household would (65G-2.009(14)(a)); the facility must not depend on resident labor and may only encourage, not require, chores (65G-2.009(1)(a)7).
Support access to competitive integrated employment as the person chooses, coordinated with the support coordinator.

policies.title: Transfer, Discharge and Termination of Services
state_specifics: Termination procedures must be consistent with Chapter 65G-3, F.A.C. (65G-2.009(3)(a)).
Before a transfer, discuss it and the reasons with the client, authorized representative, support coordinator, APD and other service providers (65G-2.009(3)(f)).
A licensee operating multiple facilities needs APD approval before moving a client between them, except in an emergency (65G-2.009(3)(h)).
On discharge, return all personal belongings, referencing the property inventory (updated 30 days before discharge) (65G-2.009(3)(i); (5)(d)1).
Client records stay with the client; keep a retained copy for 6 years (65G-2.009(5)(g)).
Report census change in writing within 5 calendar days (65G-2.009(3)(g)).

policies.title: Staff Communication and Shift Handoff
state_specifics: Maintain a system to communicate recent incidents and resident information to staff on later shifts (65G-2.009(15)(a)).

The system must include written documentation of medical or behavioral incidents and physician/therapist orders that could affect health or safety, and a procedure to ensure the information is reviewed across all shifts.
Keep communication documentation at least one year after each entry; it may be electronic and must be available to APD during inspections (65G-2.009(15)(b)).

policies.title: Medication Administration and Staff Certification
state_specifics: Give medication only in accordance with the written order or prescription of the resident's health care practitioner (65G-2.009(12)(a)).
Keep prescription medication in its original dated label container showing prescription number, directions, resident name, physician name and pharmacy address (65G-2.009(12)(b)).
Store in a locked enclosure accessible only by staff (65G-2.009(12)(c)).
Residents whose physician has deemed them capable should be encouraged to self-administer, with staff making medication available and reminding (65G-2.009(12)(d)).
Keep a current, accurate daily record of prescription and non-prescription medication per Ch. 65G-7 (65G-2.009(12)(e)).
Staff are retrained and re-verified when there is evidence of medication errors.
Report adverse reactions immediately to the prescriber or the facility's licensed medical professional; if unreachable, seek medical attention immediately (65G-2.009(12)(g)).
A hospital admission caused by a medication error is a critical incident, reported within 4 hours (65G-2.010(6)(f)3.e).
Unlicensed staff need the APD Basic Medication Administration course (6-hour initial course; 85% exam; 100% on MAR section) and validation (s. 393.506; 65G-7.004).
Revalidate oral, enteral, ophthalmic, rectal and inhaled routes annually onsite; complete the annual 2-hour in-service on medication error prevention; revalidate within 60 days before expiry.

policies.title: Nursing Oversight and Health Care Coordination
state_specifics: Chapter 65G-2 does not require a licensed nurse in a group home; unlicensed staff may administer medication under s. 393.506 after validation. Use nursing oversight where the individual's support plan, a physician order or the handbook requires it.
Keep names, addresses and phone numbers of each resident's physician and dentist in the record (65G-2.009(5)(c)2).
Ensure appropriate action after medical, dental, therapy or other health appointments, including scheduling and staff training on any changes (65G-2.009(1)(f)).
Contact the support coordinator when needed for timely medical and dental care (65G-2.009(1)(a)3).

policies.title: Health Monitoring, Seizures and Choking Risk
state_specifics: Record special instructions for carrying, lifting, positioning, bathing and meal assistance in the resident record (65G-2.009(5)(c)5).
Immediate emergency actions include calling 911, CPR for a pulseless non-breathing person, and back blows and abdominal thrusts for choking (65G-2.010(6)(d)).
Every DSP completes classroom first aid including the abdominal thrust maneuver and CPR within 90 days; at least one CPR-certified DSP is on site whenever residents are present (65G-2.008(7)(d)).
A life-threatening injury or illness is a critical incident, reported within 4 hours (65G-2.010(6)(f)3.d).
Train staff on seizure and aspiration protocols and on each resident's individual plan before working alone.

policies.title: Change of Condition and Emergency Medical Care
state_specifics: Take immediate action to resolve the emergency (911, CPR, abdominal thrusts) (65G-2.010(6)(d)).
Immediately notify the resident's legal representative and support coordinator (65G-2.010(6)(c)).
Urgent care, ER or hospital treatment for injury or sudden-onset illness is a reportable incident, due to the Regional Office within 1 calendar day (65G-2.010(6)(g)).
A life-threatening injury or illness is a critical incident: initial notice within 4 hours, completed form within 1 calendar day.
Keep emergency numbers (doctors, ambulance, Poison Control, support coordinator, Regional Office) at every phone extension (65G-2.010(1)(b)).
Staff must take immediate action on reports of a possible adverse reaction to medication.

policies.title: Death of an Individual
state_specifics: An unexpected death is a critical incident: initial notice to the Regional Office within 4 hours of awareness (phone, e-mail or APD's reporting system), with the completed Form OP 3-0006 within 1 calendar day (65G-2.010(6)(f)).
A death that is not unexpected is a reportable incident, due within 1 calendar day (65G-2.010(6)(g)1).
If abuse, neglect or exploitation is suspected, call the Florida Abuse Hotline immediately.
Notify the legal representative and support coordinator immediately (65G-2.010(6)(c)).
Return personal belongings using the property inventory; update census with APD within 5 calendar days (65G-2.009(3)(g)).
Preserve the record, video footage (critical incident) and medication records (65G-2.009(7)(b)6).

policies.title: First Aid, CPR and Emergency Response Readiness
state_specifics: Keep an American Red Cross-approved or equivalent first aid kit on the premises with unexpired contents, in a location known to and readily available to all DSPs. Store potentially toxic kit contents safely (65G-2.009(11)).

Each DSP needs a basic first aid course plus CPR certification within 90 days of providing direct services; online or computer-based courses are not acceptable (classroom, certified trainer) (65G-2.008(7)(d)).
At least one DSP with current CPR certification must be on site whenever residents are present.
Staff must be knowledgeable of facility emergency procedures (65G-2.010(1)(a)).

policies.title: Specialized and Adaptive Equipment
state_specifics: Ensure all DSPs are trained and competent in applying, monitoring and removing specialized equipment worn by residents (AFOs, braces, splints, neck collars, helmets, safety belts) (65G-2.009(13)(a)).
Ensure staff are knowledgeable in operating wheelchairs, lifts and positioning devices (65G-2.009(13)(b)).
Contact the support coordinator as soon as significant wear and tear is noticed on a resident's specialized equipment (65G-2.009(13)(c)).

policies.title: Positive Behavior Support and Behavior Plans
state_specifics: Have a written statement of policies and procedures governing staff actions to prevent or respond to problematic behaviors, including emergency procedures and reporting, consistent with s. 393.13 and Chapters 65G-4 and 65G-8 (65G-2.009(8)(a)).
Facilitate implementation of behavior plans and correctly use reactive strategy as written in each plan (65G-2.009(1)(a)1-2).
Staff are trained on each resident's behavior plan by a certified behavior analyst; document the training in the personnel record (65G-2.008(7)(f)).
Behavior analysis services plans go to the Local Review Committee chair within 5 working days after implementation (65G-4.010(1)).

Behavior-focus and intensive-behavior homes need APD designation (handbook p. 2-48). A BCBA or Ch. 490/491 licensee monitors face to face (p. 2-52). Staff need 20 contact hours in an APD-approved curriculum (or RBT, or 90 classroom ABA hours) plus APD-approved emergency procedures training, with yearly recertification (pp. 2-52 to 2-53).

policies.title: Restrictive Interventions, Reactive Strategies, Restraint and Seclusion
federal: 42 CFR 483.450 (applies to ICF/IID only; use as best practice, not as a legal citation for waiver homes)
state_specifics: Staff may not use emergency intervention that involves restraint or seclusion, or causes physical discomfort, unless certified through an APD-approved emergency procedure curriculum under Ch. 65G-8 (65G-2.009(8)(c)).
Curriculum must be at least 12 direct training hours with an 80% minimum written test; certification is valid one year (65G-8.002(2)(f),(i); (4)).

Strictly forbidden: physical or corporal punishment (hitting, slapping, pinching, pulling hair, pushing); noxious substances (pepper on tongue, ammonia, electric shock); verbal abuse; humiliation (wet or soiled clothing, dunce cap, signs); dark or locked time-out rooms; and any reactive strategy prohibited by Rule 65G-8.009 (65G-2.009(8)(d)).
Provide training on the facility policies; keep consent information in the client record (65G-8.003(1)).
Document and notify as required by 65G-8.010; internal review at least annually (65G-8.003(6)).
Ch. 65G-8 text cited here is the 2008 adoption; APD has revisions in development, so confirm current text.

policies.title: Abuse, Neglect and Exploitation Prevention and Reporting
state_specifics: Report any known or suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation immediately to the Florida Abuse Hotline, 1-800-962-2873, under ss. 39.201 and 415.1034 (65G-2.010(6)(a)).

Zero Tolerance training is required for all DSPs before providing direct services, with a refresher every 3 years; staff must demonstrate reporting procedures in theory and practice (65G-2.008(7)(c)).
Notify the legal representative and support coordinator immediately (65G-2.010(6)(c)).
DCF verified findings are critical incidents (4-hour notice) (65G-2.010(6)(f)3.i).
Cooperate with DCF and request documentation of the conclusion of the investigation (65G-2.008(5)(e)).
Residents have the right to be free from abuse, neglect and exploitation (s. 393.13(3)(a); 65G-2.009(1)(b)1).

policies.title: Reportable Incidents and Investigations
state_specifics: Use APD Incident Reporting Form OP 3-0006 (December 2025), submitted electronically to the Regional Office (65G-2.010(6)(b),(e)).

Critical incidents: initial notice within 4 hours of awareness (phone, e-mail or APD's designated system), completed form within 1 calendar day. Critical incidents include unexpected death; any sexual activity between a covered person and a resident; absence over 1 hour of a minor or adjudicated-incompetent adult; life-threatening injury or illness; hospitalization from a medication error; negative news media; arrest of a resident for a violent crime; arrest of a covered person for a disqualifying offense; a DCF verified finding; suspected or confirmed human trafficking; and a person left in a vehicle (65G-2.010(6)(f)).

Reportable incidents are due within 1 calendar day. They include a non-unexpected death; physical altercations with law enforcement contact; injury needing urgent care/ER/hospital; non-violent arrest; competent adult absent over 8 hours; suicide attempt; Baker Act or voluntary commitment; injury to a covered person caused by a resident; and sudden-onset illness needing urgent care or hospital admission (65G-2.010(6)(g)).
Follow-up measures go to the Regional Office within 5 days after the incident is reported, with ongoing follow-up until resolved (65G-2.010(6)(h)).
Keep incident reports involving the resident in the individual record (65G-2.009(5)(c)8).
Report abuse, neglect, exploitation to the Hotline first (65G-2.010(6)(a)).

policies.title: Missing Person and Elopement
state_specifics: After determining a resident is missing, staff immediately call local law enforcement and ask the officer to take a report, assign a case number and provide it, and give the facility a copy of the report when available (65G-2.010(5)(a)-(c)).
If the officer refuses a report, document the officer's name, call the law enforcement agency and ask for the Watch Commander (65G-2.010(5)(d)).
A critical incident report is required: initial notice within 4 hours for a minor or adjudicated-incompetent adult missing over 1 hour (65G-2.010(5)(e); (6)(f)3.c).
A legally competent adult missing over 8 hours is a reportable incident, due within 1 calendar day (65G-2.010(6)(g)5).
Notify the legal representative and support coordinator immediately.
Do not leave residents unattended in a vehicle (65G-2.009(14)(p)).

policies.title: Staff Named in Protective Investigations; Verified Findings and Corrective Action Plans
state_specifics: A person identified as an alleged perpetrator in an active protective investigation must not be alone with residents or have access to resident funds unless under constant visual supervision of another worker not named (65G-2.008(5)(b)).
A verified finding makes the licensee subject to disciplinary action under s. 393.0673 (65G-2.008(5)(a)).

After a verified finding against a person who remains employed, submit a Corrective Action Plan to the Regional Office within 15 days of notification of the finding. It must explain why employment is not terminated, the discipline imposed, training received (with dates) and how residents will be protected (65G-2.008(5)(c)).
If the investigation closes with no verified finding, unsupervised contact may resume (65G-2.008(5)(d)).
A verified finding by DCF is also a critical incident (4-hour notice).

policies.title: Sexual Activity, Personal Boundaries and Safety Plans
state_specifics: Develop and enforce a written sexual activity policy (also an attachment to the license application) (65G-2.009(9)(a)).
The policy must explicitly prohibit sexual activity between a resident and a covered person, and sexual activity involving residents under 18.
It may not abridge the civil and legal rights of persons with developmental disabilities under s. 393.13.

It must address staff dress code; mutual respect for personal space (knocking before entering bedrooms, except for documented visual supervision needs); who may visit whose bedroom; separate beds for all residents and DSPs; assistance with bathing, showering and toileting (staff never bathe or toilet simultaneously with a resident); supervision guidelines; and open communication to encourage reporting.
Train all DSPs on the policy (65G-2.009(9)(b)).

For homes with sexually aggressive residents or residents with a Safety Plan: DSPs review the available history; review the Safety Plan before admission; train all staff before they work with the resident; the resident or representative signs the Safety Plan; review it at least annually.

Newly placed sexually aggressive residents receive visual supervision whenever awake during the first 24 hours; they do not share a bedroom without APD approval; they are never left alone with others in a bedroom or bathroom behind closed doors without APD approval.
Minors may not possess obscene materials (s. 847.001) on the premises.
Any sexual activity between a covered person and a resident is a critical incident (4-hour notice).

policies.title: Residential Environment and Accessibility
federal: ADA Title III (28 CFR 36) as applicable
state_specifics: No mobile or manufactured homes.

Maximum 2 residents per bedroom (homes first licensed on or after 7/1/2014); at least 80 sq ft in a single room and 60 sq ft per person in a shared room; direct access from a common area; staff-only bedrooms do not count toward capacity.
One toilet, one sink and one tub/shower per 3 residents; 35 sq ft of living/dining space per household member; ventilation; design accessible to residents' disabilities.

Hot water at outlets not above 120°F; smoke and CO detectors; heating and cooling; restricted access to pools and water hazards; hazardous chemicals secured; no portable heaters in bedrooms for homes of 6 or fewer.
Bed, dresser, shelf space, window coverings and linens; residents may decorate.
Office area with secure records storage (65G-2.0072(4)).
No more than 3 APD facilities within 1,000 ft (65G-2.015(4)); homes of 6 or fewer are single-family use (s. 419.001).
Confirm each numeric standard against the full 65G-2.007 text before finalizing.

policies.title: Fire Safety, Fire Inspection and Monthly Fire Drills
state_specifics: Annually request that the local fire authority or State Fire Marshal inspect under Ch. 69A-38, F.A.C.; an approved inspection is required before an initial license or renewal (65G-2.010(2)).
Hold fire drills monthly; do not conduct required drills between midnight and 5:00 a.m. (65G-2.010(3)(b)).
Record the date, time of day, points of exit used, evacuation time and signature of the person conducting each drill; keep for one year (65G-2.010(3)(a)).
Allow Regional Office employees to observe monthly drills (65G-2.010(3)(c)).

Post emergency telephone numbers at every phone extension: law enforcement, fire department, each resident's doctors, ambulance, support coordinator, Regional Office, APD emergency on-call number, Florida Abuse Hotline and Poison Control (65G-2.010(1)(b)).
At least one telephone must be accessible to staff and residents at all times.

policies.title: Comprehensive Emergency Management Plan (CEMP), Evacuation and Emergency Shelter
state_specifics: Prepare and maintain a written CEMP under s. 393.067(8), updated as needed and at least annually (65G-2.010(4)(a)-(b)); APD supplies a CEMP template.

The CEMP must address: hazards (hurricane, tornado, flooding, fire, hazardous materials, power outage in extreme weather); care of residents who stay; care of evacuated residents (records transfer, transportation, shelter, supplies, staffing, medications); residents with mobility limits; coordination with local emergency management; post-disaster activities (family inquiries, county emergency management report); and staff assigned to each part.
Train all staff within 30 days of hire and annually after the plan's annual update (65G-2.010(4)(c)1).
Implement the plan per ss. 252.355 and 252.356, F.S. (65G-2.010(4)(c)).

If evacuated by order, report to the Regional Office within 6 hours of the order and every 6 hours until complete; provide a contact person reachable 24/7 until reoccupied; do not reoccupy until cleared (65G-2.010(4)(d)).

During a declared emergency the home may shelter people above licensed capacity if safe; report to APD within 48 hours and keep a log of names, usual address and arrival/departure dates (65G-2.010(4)(e)).

policies.title: Infection Prevention and Control
state_specifics: All staff complete an HIV/AIDS educational course within 90 days of providing direct services (65G-2.008(7)(e)).
Store potentially toxic first-aid-kit materials safely (65G-2.009(11)(b)); secure hazardous chemicals (65G-2.007).
Rule 65G-2.017 (Health Safety Standards) was repealed effective 3/26/2026. Infection control practices are set by facility policy and OSHA, not by that rule.
Keep vehicles clean and in proper working order (65G-2.009(14)(i)).
The Department of Health does not inspect APD-licensed homes.

policies.title: Food, Nutrition and Modified Diets
federal: 42 CFR 441.301(c)(4)(i) (access to food at any time)
state_specifics: Follow meal provisions in 65G-2.007 (confirm full text before finalizing).
Implement diets and directions from medical or health care professionals (65G-2.009(1)(a)1).
Train staff on changes in dietary regimens after appointments (65G-2.009(1)(f)2).
Record special instructions for assisting with meals in the resident record (65G-2.009(5)(c)5).
Residents may take part in meal preparation and grocery shopping, encouraged but not required (65G-2.009(1)(a)7).
Allow access to food and kitchen as consistent with HCBS settings rules.
Poison Control and doctor numbers must be at each phone (65G-2.010(1)(b)).

policies.title: Transportation and Vehicle Safety
state_specifics: Keep a transportation record listing each participant transported for a minimum of 12 months. It includes resident names, date and time of departure and arrival, and the driver's name and signature. Staff initial it before each departure to verify each resident is accounted for, and the driver marks each resident off on arrival (65G-2.009(14)(b)).
The driver must complete a physical inspection and visual sweep of the vehicle on arrival so no resident is left in it (65G-2.009(14)(c)). A resident left in a vehicle is a critical incident.
If transportation is contracted, assign direct care staff to perform these duties (65G-2.009(14)(d)).
Do not exceed manufacturer's seating capacity or installed seatbelts; maintain the staff-to-resident ratio; residents use seatbelts or other restraints (65G-2.009(14)(e)-(g)).
No smoking or vaping in vehicles; keep the cabin between 65 and 78°F while transporting (65G-2.009(14)(j)-(k)).
Transport at no cost to residents unless the trip exceeds 25 miles, when the excess may be charged (65G-2.009(14)(l)).

Each vehicle must have a current license plate, state-required minimum insurance, a working tagged fire extinguisher, a driver with a valid license, working seatbelts and wheelchair tie-downs where applicable, heat and A/C, and be maintained safe. Maintenance documentation is kept 12 months (65G-2.009(14)(i),(m)).
Notify APD before taking clients out of Florida (65G-2.009(14)(q)).

Drivers: no driving violations in the past 3 years relating to alcohol or drugs or any moving violation causing license suspension or revocation; update driving histories annually; obey traffic laws (65G-2.008(4)(b)).
A DSP using the 90-day supervised alternative may transport only with an experienced DSP; the experienced DSP must stay within 100 feet (65G-2.008(2)(f)2).

policies.title: Staffing Levels, Resident Supervision and Overnight Coverage
federal: FLSA 29 CFR 552, 785 (home care and sleep time rules, as applicable)
state_specifics: At least one staff person must be present at all times while residents are in the facility. The only exception is a written plan, approved by the Regional Office before implementation, allowing a specified resident to be alone for limited periods (65G-2.009(6)(b)).

The rule does not use the term 'awake overnight'; set overnight coverage by resident need, the support plan, behavior plan and Safety Plan. Newly placed sexually aggressive residents need visual supervision whenever awake in the first 24 hours (65G-2.009(9)(c)4).

Staffing must meet the pattern approved in the most recent license application and APD's factors (resident level of need, behavior plans, support plans, Safety Plans, medically ordered care, court orders, number of residents, staff competency, range of services) (65G-2.008(1)(a)).

Meet the handbook minimum direct-care hours per resident per day (Minimal 4, Moderate 6, Extensive 1 8, Extensive 2 11); the home total may be met daily or over a 7-day period. Example: 6 Moderate residents = 36 hours/day.
Do not depend on volunteers or residents to meet staffing (65G-2.009(1)(a)7).
Maintain the staff-to-resident ratio when transporting (65G-2.009(14)(f)).
Post a written weekly schedule at least one week ahead; keep actual schedules for 6 months (65G-2.008(6)(a)4).

policies.title: Background Screening and the Care Provider Background Screening Clearinghouse
state_specifics: Level 2 screening under ch. 435 and s. 393.0655 is required for the applicant, managers, supervisors, every direct service provider, and anyone with access to residents' living areas, funds or property.

Screening is done through the AHCA Care Provider Background Screening Clearinghouse (s. 435.12); use a Clearinghouse-authorized Livescan vendor. AHCA Background Screening Unit: 850-412-4503; bgscreen@ahca.myflorida.com.
Staff or volunteers who do not meet eligibility must not provide direct care or have access to any resident, funds or living setting (65G-2.008(2)(b)).
The licensee is responsible for ensuring every DSP complied; refusal to dismiss a non-compliant worker can result in license denial or revocation (s. 393.0655).
Exemptions from disqualification are only as provided in s. 435.07.
Annual (at least) check of the FDLE Sexual Offender/Predator database for registrants within one mile; notify and document staff notification (65G-2.008(4)(c)).
Arrest of a covered person for a disqualifying offense under s. 393.0655 is a critical incident (4-hour notice).

policies.title: DSP Qualifications, Hiring and Performance Evaluation
state_specifics: DSP must be at least 18, pass screening, hold a high school diploma or equivalent (official transcripts, affidavits or other formal documents may establish equivalency) (65G-2.008(2)(a)-(c)).

Before employment, a DSP needs one year of experience in a medical, psychiatric, nursing or childcare setting or working with persons with developmental disabilities, or 30 semester hours / 45 quarter hours / 720 classroom hours in special education, mental health, counseling, guidance, social work or health and rehabilitative services (65G-2.008(2)(d)).

Alternative: a DSP without the experience works the first 90 days directly under supervision of a qualified DSP under the same contiguous roof line; written notice to the Regional Office within 5 days after start (name and facility); performance evaluation within 120 days. The unqualified DSP may only take residents out with an experienced DSP staying within 100 feet (65G-2.008(2)(f)-(h)).
DSP must be mentally competent, physically capable of the duties, and not impaired by alcohol, medications or other substances (65G-2.008(3)(b)-(c); (4)(a)).
Keep DSP wages at or above the Florida minimum wage ($15.00/hr from Sept. 30, 2026).

policies.title: Direct Support Professional Orientation and Training
state_specifics: Zero Tolerance (abuse, neglect, exploitation detection, prevention and reporting): before providing direct services, then every 3 years (65G-2.008(7)(c)).
Direct Care Core Competencies (APD curriculum): within 90 days of first providing services (65G-2.008(7)(a)).
Classroom first aid, abdominal thrust and CPR: within 90 days; no online-only (65G-2.008(7)(d)).
HIV/AIDS course: within 90 days (65G-2.008(7)(e)).
Emergency management plan: within 30 days of hire and annually after the annual plan update (65G-2.010(4)(c)).
Medication administration certification and annual revalidation (65G-7.004; s. 393.506).
Each resident's behavior plan: training by a certified behavior analyst (65G-2.008(7)(f)); Safety Plan training before working with the resident (65G-2.009(9)(c)2).
Sexual activity policy training (65G-2.009(9)(b)); resident-funds procedures training for staff with access (65G-2.009(4)(b)).
Emergency intervention/reactive strategy certification before any use; valid for one year (65G-8.002(3)-(4)).
Behavior focus staff: 20 contact hours plus yearly recertification (handbook pp. 2-52 to 2-53).
Training records are kept at least 3 years and available to APD (65G-2.008(7)(b)).

policies.title: Employee Health, Fitness for Duty and Communicable Disease
federal: 29 CFR 1910.1030 (hepatitis B vaccination offer for exposed employees)
state_specifics: DSPs must not be under the influence of alcohol, medications or other substances to the extent their normal faculties are impaired (ability to see, hear, walk, talk, judge distances, drive, make judgments, act in emergencies) (65G-2.008(4)(a)).
DSPs must be physically capable of performing their duties (65G-2.008(3)(c)).

No TB test or physical exam requirement was found in Rule 65G-2.008; 65G-2.017 (Health Safety Standards) was repealed 3/26/2026. Any pre-employment TB screening is a facility policy choice and must be applied consistently, with ADA-compliant medical privacy.

policies.title: Personnel Records
state_specifics: Maintain job descriptions for paid staff, documentation of all facility staff training (dates, content, trainers, attendees) and a separate record for each full- and part-time employee. The record includes education, qualifications, experience, references, background screening, training participation and discipline (65G-2.008(6)(a)).
Keep a written weekly schedule at least one week in advance; keep schedules of actual coverage for 6 months.
Provide copies to APD within 3 calendar days of request (65G-2.008(6)(b)).
Keep training documentation at least 3 years (65G-2.008(7)(b)).
Keep the DSP 120-day performance evaluation in the file for workers hired under the supervised alternative (65G-2.008(2)(h)).
Workers' compensation is mandatory with four or more employees (s. 440.02).
Pay at least the Florida minimum wage ($15.00/hr from Sept. 30, 2026).

policies.title: Staff Conduct and Professional Boundaries
state_specifics: The licensee, employees and their family members may not be named beneficiary of a resident's life insurance unless related by blood or marriage, nor receive indirect financial benefit from it, nor borrow or use a resident's funds (65G-2.009(4)(j)).
Employees may not gain financial benefit by charging fees against or using resident funds (65G-2.009(4)(a)).
Staff follow the dress code and personal-space rules in the sexual activity policy; no sexual activity with residents; no sleeping in resident beds (65G-2.009(9)(a)).
Forbidden responses to behavior: corporal punishment, noxious substances, verbal abuse, humiliation, dark or locked time-out rooms (65G-2.009(8)(d)).
Staff must report suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation immediately to the Florida Abuse Hotline, 1-800-962-2873.
Staff may not use residents' images for solicitation without written permission (65G-2.009(10)).
Apply discipline consistently; a verified finding triggers the licensee's own discipline and a Corrective Action Plan within 15 days if the worker is retained (65G-2.008(5)).

policies.title: Individual Records and Retention
state_specifics: Maintain an individual record for each resident on the premises (may be electronic) containing information pertinent to health, supervision and care (65G-2.009(5)(a)).

Minimum contents: name and date of birth; physician and dentist name, address and phone; legal representative and support coordinator contacts; written authorization for routine medical/dental care; medical and dental reports and medication history, with special instructions for carrying, lifting, positioning, bathing and meals; legal competency, guardianship status and authorized representatives; property inventory; incident reports involving the resident; color photograph taken within the past five years; and the current support plan with any implementation plan or behavior plan (65G-2.009(5)(c)).
Update at least 30 days following new information (65G-2.009(5)(d)); property inventory every 12 months and 30 days before discharge.
Keep monthly personal funds accounting and receipts of $25 or more for at least one year (65G-2.009(4)(d)).

Keep fire drill records 1 year (65G-2.010(3)(a)); transportation records and vehicle maintenance records 12 months (65G-2.009(14)); staff communication records 1 year (65G-2.009(15)(b)); staff training records 3 years (65G-2.008(7)(b)); actual staff schedules 6 months (65G-2.008(6)(a)4).
Retain a copy of each individual's record 6 years, consistent with HIPAA. The records themselves are the client's property and follow the client on a move (65G-2.009(5)(g)).
Provide a complete copy to APD no later than 2 calendar days after request (65G-2.009(5)(f)).

policies.title: Required Reports to the State
state_specifics: Abuse, neglect, exploitation: Florida Abuse Hotline 1-800-962-2873, immediately.

Critical incidents: initial notice to the Regional Office within 4 hours; completed OP 3-0006 within 1 calendar day. Reportable incidents: within 1 calendar day. Follow-up: within 5 days after reporting, then ongoing until resolved.
Notice before accepting a new resident; census changes in writing within 5 calendar days.
Evacuation report within 6 hours of order and every 6 hours; over-capacity emergency shelter report within 48 hours.
Written notice to Regional Office within 5 days after a DSP starts under the 90-day supervised alternative; 15-day Corrective Action Plan after a verified finding retained.
Annual sworn cost statement for APD-funded clients (s. 393.067(10)).
License renewal at least 45 days before expiration; 30 days' notice before closing a home; request capacity changes 30 days ahead.
Notify APD before taking clients out of Florida.
Notify local zoning after the first resident is placed.
Providers must also keep current their APD iConnect data and Medicaid enrollment information.

forms.name: APD Incident Reporting Form OP 3-0006 (December 2025)
forms.purpose: Mandatory report of critical and reportable incidents to the Regional Office (initial notice within 4 hours for critical incidents; form within 1 calendar day); follow-up documentation.

forms.name: License Application Form 65G-2.002-A (December 2025)
forms.purpose: Initial and renewal APD facility license application, including budget sheet and required attachments.

forms.name: Medicaid Waiver Services Agreement (AHCA Form 5000-3553)
forms.purpose: Provider agreement completing iBudget waiver enrollment.

forms.name: Form 65G-13.008A (Room and Board claim)
forms.purpose: Claim APD room-and-board payment within 90 days after month end.

forms.name: Admission and Termination Criteria Statement
forms.purpose: Written criteria required by 65G-2.009(3)(a) and by the license application.

forms.name: APD New Resident Notification
forms.purpose: Notice to APD before accepting each new resident.

forms.name: Census Change Notice (written, within 5 calendar days)
